bug_semantics: sk_clone() (formerly sk_clone_lock) shallow-copies the parent socket's ->sk_bpf_storage pointer into the new socket via sock_copy(). If sk_clone() bails out early (e.g., sk_filter_charge() failure) before reaching bpf_sk_storage_clone(), newsk->sk_bpf_storage still aliases the parent socket's BPF local storage. When newsk is then freed via sk_free(), the destructor chain __sk_destruct() -> bpf_sk_storage_free() tears down and frees the PARENT socket's bpf local storage (smap elements, RCUINIT pointer), leaving the parent socket with a dangling ->sk_bpf_storage — use-after-free on the parent's storage (CWE-416).
flaw_origin: The fix commit 7cbd0c4cebe4c9f678d15e6b9ba975e1155a107f carries two Fixes tags: 6ac99e8f23d4 ("bpf: Introduce bpf sk local storage", 2019-04-26, Martin KaFai Lau) — which created sk->sk_bpf_storage and wired bpf_sk_storage_free() into __sk_destruct(), making the shallow-copied alias lethal on early bailout — and f12dd75959b0 ("bpf: net: Set sk_bpf_storage back to NULL for cloned sk", 2019-06-11, Martin KaFai Lau) — which placed the reset `RCU_INIT_POINTER(newsk->sk_bpf_storage, NULL)` inside sk_clone_lock()'s filter-charge path but before/regardless of early bailouts, and whose removal/relocation is exactly what the 2026 fix does. The pointer-capture window opened by 6ac99e8f23d4 (parent tree 3745dc24 has zero sk_bpf_storage occurrences in net/core/sock.c; the field itself is introduced there) is the primary origin; 8f51dfc73bf1 (2019-08-14, Stanislav Fomichev, clone-on-accept) replaced the inline NULL-reset with a call to bpf_sk_storage_clone() positioned after the early-bailout sites, which preserved (and operationalized) the stale-alias path the advisory describes.

evidence: Advisory (CVE-2026-68399 / GHSA-f9jq-9v6w-22v9, kernel CVN entry): 'bpf: Fix UAF in sock clone early bailouts'; sk_clone() shallow-copies ->sk_bpf_storage via sock_copy(); early bailout before bpf_sk_storage_clone() leaves newsk->sk_bpf_storage pointing at the parent's storage; sk_free() -> __sk_destruct() -> bpf_sk_storage_free() destroys the parent's storage; fix resets newsk->sk_bpf_storage to NULL immediately after sock_copy(); stable backports at git.kernel.org/stable/c/14b49b5a... (linux stable) and 7cbd0c4c... (mainline).

Fix commit 7cbd0c4cebe4c9f678d15e6b9ba975e1155a107f (2026-07-09, Matt Bobrowski <mattbobrowski@google.com>, committer Daniel Borkmann, Link: https://lore.kernel.org/bpf/20260709025316.999913-1-mattbobrowski@google.com): carries `Fixes: 6ac99e8f23d4 (\"bpf: Introduce bpf sk local storage\")` and `Fixes: f12dd75959b0 (\"bpf: net: Set sk_bpf_storage back to NULL for cloned sk\")`. Diff: net/core/sock.c moves `RCU_INIT_POINTER(newsk->sk_bpf_storage, NULL)` (now CONFIG_BPF_SYSCALL-guarded) from bpf_sk_storage_clone()'s caller region to immediately after sock_copy() in sk_clone(); net/core/bpf_sk_storage.c drops the now-redundant in-function NULL initialization.

BIC creation check: 6ac99e8f23d4 (2019-04-26) creates net/core/bpf_sk_storage.c (804 lines) and in net/core/sock.c adds `#include <net/bpf_sk_storage.h>` plus `bpf_sk_storage_free(sk)` in __sk_destruct() — the destructor wiring that makes a stale alias destructive; `git show 3745dc24:net/core/sock.c | grep -c sk_bpf_storage` = 0 (introducer_parent_absent=true for the field/chain).

Decomposed ancestry: f12dd75959b0 (2019-06-11) added the first NULL reset in sk_clone_lock()'s filter-charge path; 8f51dfc73bf1 (2019-08-14, 'bpf: support cloning sk storage on accept()') replaced it with `if (bpf_sk_storage_clone(sk, newsk)) { sk_free_unlock_clone(newsk); ... }` — `git log --all -S 'bpf_sk_storage_clone' -- net/core/bpf_sk_storage.c` pins the function's introduction there — leaving the early-bailout path (sk_filter_charge failure before this call) exposed with an aliased pointer, the exact window the advisory describes. Both are recorded in decomposed_shas as the pattern's operational ancestors.

Version boundary: BIC first ships in tag v5.2 (tag --contains head; 5.2.1 also); the flaw persists to 6.x mainline until the 2026-07-09 fix; stable backport 14b49b5ab299 is marked '[ Upstream commit 7cbd0c4cebe4... ]' in its message.

reasoning: Vulnerability first: a shallow-copied ->sk_bpf_storage pointer plus an early bailout path plus a destructor that unconditionally frees sk_bpf_storage equals parent-storage UAF; the fix's relocation of the NULL reset to immediately after sock_copy() proves the alias window is the defect. BIC choice: the primary Fixes: target 6ac99e8f23d4 introduced the storage field, the destructor wiring, and (via sock_copy()'s existing shallow copy semantics) the alias itself; its parent tree lacks the field entirely, so the BIC is the introducer. f12dd759 and 8f51dfc are recorded as decomposed ancestors that shaped the vulnerable window (first reset, then clone-call repositioning) but 6ac99e8f is the single earliest root.
